title: Regional GPU economics & capacity simulation (working sheet)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working simulation to compare $/1M tokens across regions and GPU families and to produce a monthly GPU-hour burn estimate for Reserved vs. On-demand scenarios. This is a pragmatic, numbers-first sheet for infra planning and finances to iterate on.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline reserved plan: 120 A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs in us-west => ~86,400 GPU-hours/month => ~$216k/month (assumptions below)
- Estimated $/1M tokens (13B model, 45% avg util): ~ $1.0 / 1M tokens (US-west, A100) — region and HW materially change this (EU/AP ~1.2–1.6x)
- H100 gives ~1.6–2.0x throughput for the same model in our tests; effective $/1M tokens improves but unit-hour price is higher, so net depends on throughput uplift and cache/hit patterns.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Model families and tokens/sec (inference throughput per GPU):
  - redwood-13B (quantized / optimized): A100: 1,500 tps, H100: 2,400 tps
  - redwood-65B (quantized): A100: 520 tps, H100: 820 tps
  - large-70B-class: A100: 420 tps, H100: 680 tps
- Effective utilization = fraction of wall-clock time GPU is doing useful generation work (after batching/idle/maintenance). Default: 45% baseline, 70% optimized reserved, 25% burst-on-demand.
- Average request length (generation tokens produced): 60 tokens (can be parameterized).
- Prefix/KV cache hit improvement: reduces load by effective multiplier; default: no cache benefit (0%); we run scenarios for 20% and 50% hit.
- Cost per GPU-hour (USD) by region & family (market + reserved blended):
  - A100: us-west $2.50, us-east $2.20, eu-west $2.80, ap-southeast $3.20
  - H100: us-west $3.80, us-east $3.50, eu-west $4.00, ap-southeast $4.60
  - Note: these are blended reserved/on-demand mix prices; adjust for 1yr reserved discounts.

Quick formulas (single-GPU):
- tokens_per_hour = throughput_tps * 3600 * utilization
- $/1M_tokens = (cost_per_gpu_hour) / (tokens_per_hour / 1_000_000)
- monthly_gpu_hours = GPUs_provisioned * 24 * 30
- monthly_tokens_served = monthly_gpu_hours * tokens_per_hour

Baseline example calculation (13B on A100, us-west):
- throughput_tps = 1,500 tps
- utilization = 0.45 (45%)
- tokens_per_hour = 1,500 * 3600 * 0.45 = 2,430,000 tokens/hr
- cost_per_gpu_hour = $2.50
- $/1M_tokens = 2.50 / (2.43) ≈ $1.03 per 1M tokens

Reserved fleet example (planning):
- target reserved GPUs: 120 A100 (baseline)
- monthly_gpu_hours = 120 * 24 * 30 = 86,400 GPU-hours
- monthly_cost (us-west) = 86,400 * $2.50 = $216,000
- monthly_tokens = 86,400 * 2,430,000 = 210,067,200,000 tokens (~210B tokens)
- implied $/1M tokens = 216,000 / 210,067.2 ≈ $1.03 / 1M tokens (same as single-GPU calc, sanity check)

Region sensitivity (13B, utilization 45%, 120 GPUs):
- us-east (A100 $2.20): monthly_cost = 86,400 * 2.20 = $190,080 => $/1M ≈ $0.90
- eu-west (A100 $2.80): monthly_cost = 86,400 * 2.80 = $241,920 => $/1M ≈ $1.15
- ap-southeast (A100 $3.20): monthly_cost = 276,480 => $/1M ≈ $1.32

HW substitution impact (replace A100 with H100, same GPU count, 13B):
- H100 throughput uplift ~1.6x (2,400 tps) but cost/hour up ~1.52x ($3.80/$2.50)
- tokens_per_hour (H100) = 2,400 * 3600 * 0.45 = 3,888,000 tokens/hr
- $/1M_tokens (H100 us-west) = 3.80 / (3.888) ≈ $0.98 per 1M tokens -> slight improvement
- Conclusion: H100 helps if throughput uplift ratio > price_ratio; also H100 helps more at low-latency regimes where fewer GPUs needed for same tail latency.

Utilization sensitivity (13B, us-west A100):
- Util 25% => tokens/hr = 1,350,000 => $/1M = 2.50 / 1.35 ≈ $1.85
- Util 45% => $/1M ≈ $1.03 (baseline)
- Util 70% => tokens/hr = 3,780,000 => $/1M = 2.50 / 3.78 ≈ $0.66
- Note: utilization has larger impact than small regional price shifts; operational focus should be increasing sustained util (batching, caching, multi-tenant packing).

Example burst (on-demand autoscale) costs:
- If we keep 40 reserved GPUs and autoscale +80 GPUs on-demand at 25% util during peaks:
  - reserved monthly hours = 40 * 24 * 30 = 28,800 => reserved cost (us-west A100) = 28,800 * 2.50 = $72,000
  - on-demand monthly hours (assume average 6 hours/day of burst) = 80 * 6 * 30 = 14,400 => on-demand price multiplier 1.4x => on-demand cost = 14,400 * (2.50 * 1.4) = $50,400
  - total = $122,400, tokens served adjusted by util differences -> recompute $/1M if needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run microbenchmarks (13B/65B/70B) on latest runtime kernel set for accurate tps numbers (action: @Aisha).
- Capture reserved 1yr & 3yr price decks from cloud partners and plug into region table (action: @Priya).
- Add cache-hit model: multi-tenant prefix reuse reduces effective tokens served by X% — model scenarios for 20% and 50% hit.
- Tail-latency vs throughput trade: how many GPUs needed for 99.9% latency SLO at target QPS? Need end-to-end perf curves.

Housekeeping notes (notes-to-self style):
- This sheet is intentionally rough — we'll port to a formal Google Sheet if numbers stabilize.
- Link draft -> Confluence page (see linked_artifacts) and add finance owner for monthly projection.

Appendix: quick scenario table (single-GPU $/1M tokens)
- 13B / A100 / us-west / util45 => ~ $1.03 / 1M
- 13B / A100 / eu-west / util45 => ~ $1.15 / 1M
- 13B / H100 / us-west / util45 => ~ $0.98 / 1M
- 65B / A100 / us-west / util45 => throughput 520 tps => tokens/hr=842,400 => $/1M = 2.50 / 0.8424 ≈ $2.97 / 1M
- 65B / H100 / us-west / util45 => throughput 820 tps => tokens/hr=1,327,200 => $/1M = 3.80 / 1.3272 ≈ $2.86 / 1M

Quick notes for presentation to finance/engineering:
- Focus bullets: (1) utilization lifting and cache yield > region swap for largest gains, (2) H100 adoption shows modest $/1M improvements for gen-heavy workloads; justify by tail-latency and density gains, (3) reserved commit sizing should be informed by target 95th percentile sustained QPS not absolute peak.

Changelog: 2026-02-20 initial draft, 2026-03-05 updated with H100 microbenchmarks and autoscale example.

Questions for reviewers (please add inline):
- Are these blended GPU-hour costs aligned with procurement numbers? If not, add actuals.
- Any objections to using 45% baseline util for planning or should we target 55% for 2026 roadmap?

End of sheet.
